column12: description

A cluster receives a label only when its adjusted marker score clears both background and the next-best candidate by this margin. Increase it to leave ambiguous clusters unassigned rather than forcing a label.

The selected libraries share normalization, clustering and multimodal integration within one aggregation. These identifiers must match active rows in the GEM-well table, and all selected libraries must use the same Cell Ranger reference.

Used to score cells, assign cluster labels and generate marker plots. Choose genes appropriate for the tissue and reference; a trailing minus sign marks a gene expected to be absent from that cell type.
Adds donor phenotypes and covariates to cell metadata for plotting, batch correction and downstream comparisons. Each donor assigned to a cell must have exactly one matching donor_id row.
Determines whether the pipeline constructs targets for this analysis. Deactivate unused examples or analyses before requesting all targets; this does not delete results already on disk.
Each enabled module needs a matching entry in its own configuration file; leave modules disabled until the main results have been reviewed.

Applied to nuclei after peak-based measurements become available. Each expression describes cells to remove, not retain; exclusions affect the subsequent ATAC embedding and multimodal analysis. Pipeline helpers parse each expression and evaluate it with dplyr::filter().

Used to organize motif-accessibility summaries by expected cell type. Use it to inspect regulatory programs alongside gene-expression annotations; motif accessibility is not a direct measurement of transcription-factor expression.

Harmony reduces the effects associated with these metadata columns before the embeddings are used for clustering. Use measured batch variables supported by the QC plots, since correcting a variable can also remove biological differences associated with it. Leaving this unset skips the shared Harmony correction. Passed through the Harmony helper to harmony::RunHarmony(vars_use = ...); multiple columns are combined into one interaction-batch variable first.

Used for batch correction and GEX neighbor-graph construction. Choose components supported by the PCA QC plots; including more can retain finer structure but also technical variation. GEX UMAP component selection is configured separately. The final requested component sets BPCells::svds(k = ...) in the native backend; selected embedding columns are then supplied to harmony::RunHarmony(data_mat = ...) and BPCells::knn_hnsw().

The alternatives differ in memory use and computation, so review the GEX QC results after switching rather than assuming identical embeddings. Selects Seurat::SCTransform() followed by the local dense PCA helper, or BPCells::sctransform_pearson() followed by BPCells::svds().

Variation associated with these metadata columns is removed during GEX preprocessing. Use it for effects you deliberately want to suppress, such as cell-cycle differences; it can also remove biology correlated with those variables. Leaving it unset disables this regression. Passed through the preprocessing helper to Seurat::SCTransform(vars.to.regress = ...), or used to select the covariate matrix supplied as BPCells::regress_out(latent_data = ...).

Acts on individual scDblFinder calls before the accepted GEX results pass to downstream steps, including peak calling. Disable removal when you want to inspect the calls before deciding on a filtering policy.

Drops entire GEX clusters dominated by doublet calls, including cells not individually called as doublets. This is separate from individual-cell removal and can remove a whole putative population; review the cluster evidence before tightening it. Leaving it unset disables this cluster filter.

column3: Cell-type groups for GEX doublet detection
column12: Lets scDblFinder treat related annotations as one broader population. This changes the grouping used by the detector without replacing the original cell-type labels in the analysis. The helper converts this mapping to per-cell group labels passed to scDblFinder::scDblFinder(clusters = ...).
Their chromatin-state annotations are attached to the accessible peaks. Choose tissues relevant to the sample to put accessible regions in regulatory context; leaving this unset skips the annotation.

Used for ATAC batch correction and neighbor-graph construction. Inspect component associations with technical metrics when deciding which to retain; ATAC UMAP component selection is configured separately. The final requested component sets BPCells::svds(k = ...); selected embedding columns are then supplied to harmony::RunHarmony(data_mat = ...) and BPCells::knn_hnsw().

Determines whether a fragment contributes through its insertion sites or its overlap with a peak. The choice changes the accessibility matrix used for downstream QC and analysis, so comparisons between runs should use a consistent counting definition. Passed directly to BPCells::peak_matrix(mode = ...) for the consensus matrix and through a helper for blacklist-region counts.

Runs within the configured cell groups before their regions are combined into a consensus peak set. Changing the caller can alter peak boundaries and coverage, affecting the peak matrix and downstream ATAC analyses. Selects an external macs3 callpeak command or BPCells::call_peaks_tile() through the peak-calling helpers.

The selected metadata column also organizes differential-accessibility comparisons. Broader groups pool more coverage, while finer groups can reveal population-specific regions but may have less support.

Appended to the shared Harmony variables when correcting ATAC embeddings. Use it when ATAC QC reveals technical structure that needs correction beyond the variables already chosen for both modalities. The combined variables reach harmony::RunHarmony(vars_use = ...) through the helper, which combines multiple columns into an interaction batch.
Acts on individual scDblFinder calls before the accepted ATAC results pass to multimodal integration. Disable removal to inspect the calls before committing to an ATAC filtering policy.

Drops entire ATAC clusters with excessive doublet calls, including their individually unflagged cells. This acts separately from individual-cell removal; review whether a flagged cluster is a doublet population or a plausible cell type. Leaving it unset disables this cluster filter.

Higher values generally produce finer groups; review marker consistency and population size when choosing a resolution for annotation and peak calling. Passed through clustering helpers to igraph::cluster_leiden(resolution = ...).

Higher values generally split populations more finely; review motif patterns and agreement with expression-derived labels when choosing a resolution. Passed through clustering helpers to igraph::cluster_leiden(resolution = ...).

Higher values generally produce finer multimodal groups, which become the populations used in many downstream summaries and comparisons. Passed through WNN clustering helpers to igraph::cluster_leiden(resolution = ...).
Cells in clusters below this threshold are excluded from downstream metadata and subsequent processing. Raising it can remove rare biological populations as well as unstable groups.

Smaller neighborhoods emphasize local structure, while larger ones connect cells across broader regions of the embedding; this is separate from the UMAP neighborhood setting. Passed through neighbor-graph helpers to BPCells::knn_hnsw(k = ...) and to the local weighted-neighbor construction for WNN.
Shown on UMAPs and composition plots. Use these views to compare batches, donor groups or study conditions across the inferred populations; the columns must already exist in cell metadata.
Shown as numerical annotations on UMAPs. These views help locate phenotype or technical gradients within the embedding without using those variables to define the clusters.

Smaller values emphasize local separation and larger values broader organization; changing this setting changes the layout, not the separately computed clustering graph. Passed through embedding helpers to uwot::umap(n_neighbors = ...), capped by the available cells or retained WNN neighbors.

Smaller values allow nearby cells to pack more tightly in the layout; apparent separation is not independent evidence for distinct cell types. Passed through embedding helpers to uwot::umap(min_dist = ...).

Use the LSI QC results to exclude components dominated by unwanted technical variation; this does not change the separate component selection for clustering. The helper selects these embedding columns before passing the resulting matrix to uwot::umap(X = ...).

Use the PCA QC results to select the structure you want to visualize; this does not change the separate component selection for clustering. The helper selects these embedding columns before passing the resulting matrix to uwot::umap(X = ...).
Use these plots to inspect candidate genes or pathways without adding them to the annotation signatures or changing the assigned cell-type labels.

Compare relative abundance between donors while accounting for the specified covariates and contrasts. Donor or GEM-well filters define the analysis population; restricting the cell types tested does not change the composition denominator. Use biological replication to distinguish condition effects from donor differences. The helper adds the cell-type count response to the supplied formula before fitting it with glmmTMB::glmmTMB(formula = ...); the design is constructed with stats::model.matrix().

Use counts aggregated within cell type and donor, with the specified covariates and named contrasts. Use it to test expression or accessibility differences with donors as biological replicates rather than treating individual cells as independent samples. Model formulas are converted through helpers to stats::model.matrix(); count-model design matrices are supplied to edgeR::voomLmFit(design = ...), with contrasts tested downstream.

Genes with Open Targets evidence for this disease or trait are highlighted in the figures. This adds genetic context to the display without changing the differential-analysis model or its significance estimates.

Excludes cluster-donor samples with insufficient ATAC coverage from motif-family comparisons. Raising it favors better-supported samples but can reduce donor replication or remove sparse cell types from the analysis.

Provides covariates needed by the differential-analysis models beyond those already used in the aggregation. It must preserve unique donor_id identifiers matching the analysis; when omitted, the module uses the aggregation's donor metadata table.

Their fine-mapping evidence is related to chromatin accessibility to investigate trait-associated cell populations. Study names label downstream results; supported GCST accessions are resolved through Open Targets, while local sources use prepared Parquet files.

Applied to credible-set variants before their evidence is assigned to accessible peaks. A stricter cutoff concentrates analysis on better-supported variants but discards more uncertainty from the fine-mapping results.
Use these groupings to keep large figures readable; they do not change the underlying enrichment calculations.

Higher values keep propagation closer to the seed cells; lower values allow enrichment signals to spread farther through the graph. Passed to the local random-walk implementation as restart_prob, not to an external SCAVENGE package function.

Caps the cells selected from high gchromVAR scores to initiate network propagation. This is a cap rather than a guaranteed seed count, because cells must also satisfy the seed-selection criteria. Passed to the local get_SCAVENGE_seed_index(seed_percent = ...) helper, not to an external SCAVENGE package function.
The highest-ranked candidates in each cell group are shown in scatter and genomic-track figures. It controls the display workload, not how many associations are tested.

Selects GWAS and cell-type combinations for detailed variant and coverage figures using positive deviation and a minimum enrichment z-score in either analysis route. This limits expensive plotting work; it is a descriptive screen, not a significance threshold.

Applied before statistical testing to require sufficient expression, accessibility and shared donor support. Stricter presets prioritize better-measured links but reduce coverage of sparse signals; they do not themselves establish a regulatory relationship.
